newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators ask Kohl to aid Holocaust survivors.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators ask Kohl to aid Holocaust survivors.

text.p: Eighty-three U.S. senators have signed a letter to German Chancellor Helmut Kohl protesting his government's "continued refusal" to pay pensions to thousands of elderly Holocaust survivors living in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union.

The letter, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, said the senators were concerned that survivors were not receiving pensions "even as generous 'war victims pensions' are paid to veterans of the Waffen-SS and other Nazi military organisations living in these same countries and elsewhere."

The letter comes just a week before a delegation of Jewish leaders is scheduled to fly to Bonn in what delegation members describe as a last-ditch effort to convince the German government to change its policy.
The senators' letter was organised by Connecticut Democrat Christopher Dodd and Texas Republican Kay Bailey Hutchison.
Among the signers were Senate Majority leader Trent Lott of Mississippi and Minority leader Tom Daschle of South Dakota.
Holocaust survivors in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union, unlike their counterparts in the west, receive no pensions from the German government, the letter said.
It added, "In stark contrast, many veterans of various Nazi military forces, who are living around the world, are eligible for supplemental pensions."

The letter told Kohl: "Your government recently confirmed that over 3,000 veterans of various Nazi military forces or their dependents currently living in the United States receive such pensions. German law even permits Nazi war criminals inside of Germany to receive these benefits."

World Jewish Congress executive director Elan Steinberg praised Hutchison and Dodd for organising the letter, saying it called on Germany "to address the moral and material needs of victims of Nazi persecution."
